title: Using unencrypted SQS queues is security-sensitive
description: Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) queues can be configured with server-side encryption to protect message data at rest and in transit. When SQS queues are created without encryption, sensitive message content becomes vulnerable to unauthorized access, data breaches, and compliance violations. Unencrypted queues expose message data to potential interception and unauthorized access, especially in shared or multi-tenant environments. This security risk is particularly critical when processing personally identifiable information (PII), financial data, or other sensitive business information through SQS messages.
message: Make sure that using unencrypted SQS queues is safe here.

impact.security: High impact as unencrypted SQS queues can expose sensitive message data to unauthorized access and potential data breaches
impact.reliability: Low impact on system reliability, but high risk of compliance violations and data exposure incidents

recommendation: Enable server-side encryption for SQS queues using AWS Key Management Service (KMS) customer managed keys (CMK) or AWS managed keys. Configure encryption at queue creation time and ensure all message producers and consumers are properly configured to handle encrypted queues.

noncompliant.description: Creating SQS queue without encryption using boto3
AWS CDK SQS queue without encryption
noncompliant.code:
from aws_cdk import aws_sqs as sqs
from aws_cdk import core

class MyStack(core.Stack):
    def __init__(self, scope: core.Construct, id: str, **kwargs) -> None:
        super().__init__(scope, id, **kwargs)
        
        # Noncompliant: SQS queue without encryption
        queue = sqs.Queue(
            self, "MyQueue",
            queue_name="my-queue",
            visibility_timeout=core.Duration.seconds(60)
        )

compliant.description: Creating SQS queue with AWS managed KMS encryption
compliant.code:
import boto3

# Compliant: SQS queue with AWS managed KMS encryption
sqs = boto3.client('sqs')
queue_url = sqs.create_queue(
    QueueName='my-secure-queue',
    Attributes={
        'VisibilityTimeoutSeconds': '60',
        'MessageRetentionPeriod': '1209600',
        'KmsMasterKeyId': 'alias/aws/sqs',  # AWS managed key
        'KmsDataKeyReusePeriodSeconds': '300'
    }
)

compliant.description: AWS CDK SQS queue with customer managed KMS key
compliant.code:
from aws_cdk import aws_sqs as sqs
from aws_cdk import aws_kms as kms
from aws_cdk import core

class MyStack(core.Stack):
    def __init__(self, scope: core.Construct, id: str, **kwargs) -> None:
        super().__init__(scope, id, **kwargs)
        
        # Create customer managed KMS key
        kms_key = kms.Key(
            self, "MyQueueKey",
            description="KMS key for SQS queue encryption"
        )
        
        # Compliant: SQS queue with customer managed KMS encryption
        queue = sqs.Queue(
            self, "MySecureQueue",
            queue_name="my-secure-queue",
            visibility_timeout=core.Duration.seconds(60),
            encryption=sqs.QueueEncryption.KMS,
            encryption_master_key=kms_key
        )

compliant.description: Using specific customer managed KMS key ARN
compliant.code:
import boto3

# Compliant: SQS queue with specific KMS key ARN
sqs = boto3.client('sqs')
kms_key_arn = "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012"

queue_url = sqs.create_queue(
    QueueName='my-encrypted-queue',
    Attributes={
        'KmsMasterKeyId': kms_key_arn,
        'KmsDataKeyReusePeriodSeconds': '300'
    }
)

compliant.description: Queue with proper encryption and access policy

devsecops.remediation_guidance: Enable SQS server-side encryption with KMS

why_is_this_an_issue: Amazon SQS queues without encryption expose sensitive message data to potential security risks. When messages are stored in unencrypted queues, they are vulnerable to unauthorized access from malicious actors who might gain access to the underlying storage infrastructure. This creates compliance risks for organizations handling sensitive data and violates security best practices for cloud-based message queuing systems. The lack of encryption also makes it difficult to meet regulatory requirements such as GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI DSS that mandate encryption of sensitive data at rest and in transit.

how_to_fix.description: Identify all SQS queue creation and configuration code in your application
Choose an appropriate KMS key: AWS managed key (alias/aws/sqs) or customer managed key for better control
For boto3 clients, add 'KmsMasterKeyId' to the queue attributes during creation
For AWS CDK, set the encryption property to QueueEncryption.KMS and specify the encryption_master_key
Update IAM policies to include necessary KMS permissions for queue encryption/decryption
Test queue operations to ensure encryption doesn't break existing message processing logic
Update monitoring and logging to account for encrypted queue operations
